context:
Goal: a wording change you ruled reaches main fast, without costing other work more than it gains.
Problem (rule): you ruled that a ruled wording change skips the batch queue, but not whether it may cancel a batch already running CI, which only merge and CI fixes may do.
Based on (ruling): R55 (13:21 CST Nov 12): a merge-flow or CI fix cancels a running batch and goes first; a lane outside that list does not.
Based on (ruling): R59 part 3: a stored ruling governs sessions and guards at once, before its wording reaches main.
Departs from: main has no express route for ruled wording — the change adds one; this pick sets whether it may cancel a running batch.

options.gain: No batch loses its CI run; the ruling already governs from the store meanwhile.
options.how: The wording change goes next after the running batch's CI ends; nothing is cancelled.
options.label: Wait for the running batch (Recommended)
options.lose: The wording reaches main up to one batch run later.

options.gain: The wording reaches main at once.
options.how: The batch runner cancels the running batch, merges the wording change, then reruns the batch.
options.label: Cancel the batch, as merge fixes do
options.lose: The cancelled batch reruns its full CI, delaying every lane in it.

ref: PR #2985 (ruled prose skips the batch queue); lane question 16:06 CST
short: Ruled wording vs a running batch
title: Should a ruled wording change cancel a batch that is already in CI?
why: Cancelling a batch costs a full CI rerun, and your ruling on merge fixes covers only those.
